trust_decision.summary: The trust boundary is the finished kubectl/helm argv: 18 MCP tools push caller-supplied strings (resourceType, name, nodeName, helm release/chart, args) into positional or flag slots, and the only check at the pinned commit (assertNoDangerousFlags) is wired into kubectl_generic alone, inspecting just its flags object and args array; the fix moves the decision to exec time by validating every token of the final argv inside a shared execFileSyncSafe wrapper.

landing_point.why: The only existing protection, and the module whose comment describes the exfiltration surface; an engineer reading 'argument injection exposes cluster credentials' lands on assertNoDangerousFlags and sees it only inspects the flags object and args array of kubectl_generic (called once, src/tools/kubectl-generic.ts:77), never the positional slots the other tools build.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: port_forward is a long-running streaming feature that spawns kubectl (a different primitive, no --context support, schema fields resourceType/resourceName/localPort/targetPort only), so a solver can call it a neighbouring feature the report's name/flags PoC does not describe and the shared execFileSync wrapper never sees.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every tool legitimately emits '--context <value>' from the caller's optional context parameter, and 'context' is in DANGEROUS_FLAGS; a fix that reuses assertNoDangerousFlags over the whole argv rejects every context-carrying call and breaks normal multi-cluster use. A second over-broad edge is exec_in_pod, whose container command is appended after a literal '--' (src/tools/exec_in_pod.ts:115): tokens like 'myapp --server=...' or 'ls -s' are not kubectl flags but a whole-argv scan rejects them.

O6_input_shapes: dangerous flag in a bare positional slot (name / resourceType / nodeName / helm release or chart), e.g. name = '--server=https://attacker'
joined form '--server=value' as a single token
split form '--server' 'value' (token scan catches the flag token regardless of position)
short alias '-s' appearing as its own argv token anywhere
flag tokens repeated as values of legitimate flags are still scanned (whole-argv scan), while non-'-' tokens and non-string tokens are ignored

O8_uncovered_routes.route: port_forward spawns kubectl with `${resourceType}/${resourceName}` pushed into the port-forward positional slot and only '-n namespace' before it; no argv guard runs, so resourceType='--server=https://attacker' becomes a kubectl flag that redirects the call and leaks the operator token.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different transport (spawn for a long-lived process, no execFileSync), different feature, and the report's example fields do not appear in its schema.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: One directory across from the landing point (src/security -> src/tools), separate file; src/tools/port_forward.ts:10.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A streaming kubectl tool (watch/top/attach) that assembles argv and calls spawn() directly, bypassing execFileSyncSafe.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainers already wrote exactly this for port-forward because long-running processes cannot use execFileSync; any new streaming tool copies the pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second in-file argv builder (pods lookup by label selector) that calls execFileSync on its own.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Five separate execFileSync call sites already exist in this one file, so adding a sixth lookup helper without the wrapper is a natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared executeKubectlCommand helper reused by a new kubectl subcommand with caller-supplied positionals.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Adding an operation means only appending args to this helper; a copy of the helper that skipped the guard would look harmless.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared 'withContext' argv builder that stamps '--context <value>' onto every tool's args array.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: contextParameter is already shared by every tool; centralising argv assembly there is an obvious refactor and must preserve the context exception.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new helm subcommand run through the generic executeCommand(command, args) helper with a caller-supplied release/chart positional.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper takes the binary as a variable and is reused for helm, kubectl and cat, so new helm commands are one args array away.

O9_family: Argument/flag injection (CWE-88) into kubectl and helm argv, leading to API-server redirection and bearer-token exfiltration.

O10_build.toolchain: tsc 5.6.2 via `npm run build` (package.json:19), vitest 2.1.9 via `npm run test` (package.json:23), bun lockfile (bun install / bun run)
services: Kubernetes cluster (minikube) for the integration suites
O10_build.project_tests: tests/kubectl-flags-security.unit.test.ts is a pure unit suite (guard throws before exec, uses printf/false) and runs offline; tests/kubectl.test.ts, tests/kubectl-generic.test.ts, tests/helm.test.ts, tests/exec_in_pod.test.ts and tests/port_forward.test.ts are cluster-backed integration suites (CI starts minikube, .github/workflows/ci.yml:22-28).

j.j_sites_touched: src/security/kubectl-flags.ts, src/tools/exec_in_pod.ts, src/tools/helm-operations.ts, src/tools/kubectl-apply.ts, src/tools/kubectl-context.ts, src/tools/kubectl-create.ts, src/tools/kubectl-delete.ts, src/tools/kubectl-describe.ts, src/tools/kubectl-generic.ts, src/tools/kubectl-get.ts, src/tools/kubectl-logs.ts, src/tools/kubectl-operations.ts, src/tools/kubectl-patch.ts, src/tools/kubectl-rollout.ts, src/tools/kubectl-scale.ts, src/tools/node-management.ts
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call assertNoDangerousFlags(undefined, args) instead of raw execFileSync at all 25 call sites, which rejects the legitimate --context every tool emits (and the post-'--' container command in exec_in_pod) while still leaving the spawn-based port_forward route open.

out_of_scope_notes: helm-operations passes a caller-supplied valuesFile to `cat` (src/tools/helm-operations.ts:210), an arbitrary-file-read concern outside this advisory's credential-redirect protection; not pursued.
The ALLOW_KUBECTL_UNSAFE_FLAGS=true env escape hatch (src/security/kubectl-flags.ts:47-49) is documented, intended operator behaviour, not a bypass of this advisory.
